beats.note: Sabeer Bhatia and Jack Smith had pitched a free web email service to Draper Fisher Jurvetson in 1995. The firm wondered how they would attract members.

beats.text: Tim Draper wanted every email to carry an advert.
beats.note: He suggested a plug at the bottom of every outgoing message. The founders resisted, then agreed to the plug but not the P.S. I love you part.

beats.text: The line everyone quotes may not be what shipped.
beats.note: TechCrunch says the founders dropped the P.S. I love you wording. Another account says that exact line was appended for years. The sources disagree.

beats.context: Subscribers in the first year and a half, on less than $500,000 of marketing, according to Jurvetson and Draper's Viral Marketing article.

beats.text: The first million took about six months.
beats.note: TechCrunch's excerpt from Viral Loop says Hotmail reached 1 million users within six months of launch.

beats.text: By February 1999 Hotmail had more than 30 million active members.
beats.note: Microsoft's own release said new sign ups frequently topped 1 million a week.

beats.text: Every email sent was an advert for the service.
